questions.context: Simón estudia tercer grado en un colegio de Pereira y se presenta en clase de inglés.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Is goes with he, she and it; with I we use am.
Incorrect. Are goes with you, we and they; with I we use am.
Incorrect. Be is the base form of the verb; in a sentence with I it changes to am.
Correct. With I the verb to be is always am: I am a student.

questions.explanation: El pronombre "I" (yo) siempre va con "am": "I am a student" (yo soy estudiante). "Is" es para he, she, it y "are" para you, we, they.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Gabriela presenta a sus dos mejores amigas del barrio en Barranquilla.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Is is for one person; Lucia and Marta are two people, like they.
Correct. Lucia and Marta are two people (they), and they goes with are.
Incorrect. Am is only for I, and here the subject is Lucia and Marta.
Incorrect. Be is the base form; with two people we must use are.

questions.explanation: Lucia y Marta son dos personas, es decir "they" (ellas). Con "they" usamos "are": "Lucia and Marta are my friends".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence about the dog is correct?
questions.context: La familia Pérez tiene un perro café en su finca cerca de Fusagasugá.

options.feedback: Correct. A dog is it, and it goes with is.
Incorrect. Are is for you, we and they, not for it.
Incorrect. Am is only for I; with it we use is.
Incorrect. Be is the base form and does not change for it; the correct form is is.

questions.explanation: Para animales y cosas usamos "it", y con "it" va "is": "It is brown" (es café). "Am" es solo para I y "are" para you, we y they.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: It is Sunday. Complete: "We ____ at school today."
questions.context: Es domingo en Medellín y los niños no van al colegio.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Isn't is the negative for he, she and it; with we we use aren't.
Correct. Aren't is are + not, the negative for we: we aren't at school.
Incorrect. Am not is the negative only for I, not for we.
Incorrect. Not alone is not enough; the sentence needs a form of to be like are + not.

questions.explanation: Para negar con "we" usamos "are not", que se contrae como "aren't". Como es domingo, decimos "We aren't at school today" (hoy no estamos en el colegio).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: En el primer día de clases en Valledupar, un niño quiere saber quién es la profesora.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Are goes with you, we and they; she needs is.
Incorrect. The word order is wrong: questions with to be start with the verb.
Correct. Questions with to be put the verb first: Is she...?
Incorrect. Am is only for I, and the subject here is she.

questions.explanation: Para preguntar con el verbo to be ponemos el verbo al inicio: "Is she your teacher?". Con "she" va "is"; "am" es solo para I y "are" para you, we, they.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Después de jugar en el parque en Ibagué, la mamá le pregunta a Felipe cómo se siente.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Felipe talks about himself, so he must say I am, not you are.
Incorrect. I goes with am, so the short answer is Yes, I am.
Correct. The question is about Felipe, and I'm not is I am + not.
Incorrect. Aren't is for we, you and they; with I the negative is I'm not.

questions.explanation: Si te preguntan "Are you...?" respondes sobre ti: "Yes, I am" o "No, I'm not". "I'm not" es la forma corta de "I am not". Nunca decimos "I is" ni "I aren't".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read Pablo's text: "My name is Pablo. I am from Cali. My sisters is nine years old."
How do you correct the mistake?
questions.context: Pablo vive en Cali y escribe un texto corto sobre su familia para la clase de inglés.

options.text: My sisters are nine years old.
options.feedback: Correct. Sisters is plural (they), so the verb must be are, not is.
Incorrect. "I am from Cali" was already correct; I goes with am, not is.
Incorrect. "My name is Pablo" was already correct; name is one thing, so it uses is.
Incorrect. I goes with am; are is for you, we and they.

questions.explanation: El error está en "My sisters is": "sisters" es plural (they), así que va "are": "My sisters are nine years old". Las frases "My name is Pablo" e "I am from Cali" ya estaban bien.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "Tom and Lina are in Bogota. It is cold. Lina isn't happy because she is cold."
Which sentence is true and correct?
questions.context: Tom y Lina visitan Bogotá en julio y sienten mucho frío en Monserrate.

options.text: Tom and Lina is in Bogota.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Tom and Lina are two people, so the verb must be are, not is.
Incorrect. The text says "It is cold", so saying it isn't cold is false.
Incorrect. The text says Lina isn't happy, so this sentence is false.
Correct. The text says Lina isn't happy because she is cold.

questions.explanation: Hay que revisar dos cosas: si la oración dice lo mismo que el texto y si el verbo está bien. "Lina isn't happy" es verdadera y correcta. "Tom and Lina is" tiene error porque son dos personas.
questions.subject: ingles
